title: Theory Foundations: Notes, Rests & Beats
welcome_lead: Master the building blocks of written music — note values, rests and time signatures that every musician needs.

concepts.def: Whole note worth 4 beats — open oval, no stem.
Half note worth 2 beats — open oval with a stem.
Quarter note worth 1 beat — filled oval with a stem.
Eighth note worth half a beat — crotchet with a tail.
Sixteenth note worth a quarter beat — two tails.
Two numbers showing beats per bar and beat type.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The basic hierarchy: semibreve = 4 beats, minim = 2 beats, crotchet = 1 beat, quaver = ½ beat, semiquaver = ¼ beat.

Each note is half the value of the one above. Every note has an equivalent rest (silent value of the same length).

The top number tells you how many beats are in each bar. The bottom number tells you what kind of beat (4 = crotchet, 8 = quaver).

So 4/4 = four crotchets per bar, 3/4 = three crotchets (waltz), 6/8 = six quavers grouped in two threes (jig).

A dot after a note adds half its value. So a dotted minim = 2 + 1 = 3 beats; a dotted crotchet = 1 + ½ = 1½ beats.

A tie joins two notes of the same pitch into one longer sound — useful when a note must cross a bar line.
